title: MVMD: share mode frequencies across multiple channels
summary: MVMD couples channel-specific mode spectra through shared center frequencies. The modes can have different amplitudes and phases in each channel.

steps.title: Align the channels
steps.text: Supply measurements on a common time grid and prepare their mirrored spectra.

steps.title: Update channel spectra
steps.text: Each channel fits a mode around the current shared center.

steps.title: Pool spectral energy
steps.text: Update each center using the spectral energy from all channels, then repeat.

steps.title: Recover mode stacks
steps.text: Invert the spectra and retain the (mode,time,channel) organization before application-specific grouping.

parameters.name: K and alpha
parameters.effect: The teaching run uses three modes and bandwidth penalty 1500.

parameters.name: Upstream trace settings
parameters.effect: Uniform initialization, tau=0, and max_iter=60 bound this PySDKit demonstration; not all are public DeTime parameters.

parameters.name: primary_period / mode groups
parameters.effect: Controls DeTime's assignment of the returned modes to output components.

cautions: The optional backend requires aligned multichannel input and an explicitly checked axis convention.
PySDKit's all-axis FFT shift changes the internal channel order; its final inverse shift restores input order. The animation applies that same restoration to every displayed iterate.
A shared mode center does not identify a shared causal source, and tau=0 can leave reconstruction error.
trace_note: Captured PySDKit 0.5.0 joint solver arrays on input shaped (channel,time). Internal channels correspond to input indexes [2, 0, 1] (zero-based); applying indexes [1, 2, 0] restores original order in every displayed spectrum and mode. The final trace is checked against the upstream returned modes.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.
